# Summary

Require unique canonical IDs among Current original Atoms

```yaml
graph_rule_type: value_constraint
applies_to:
  node: "Entity/Node/Continuant/Selection//Current Original Atoms"
  property: "Entity/Node/Continuant/Atom.ID"
condition:
  unique: true
```

## Details

The `value_constraint` mapping is proposed only. [CA-D-637@5](../../07_delivery/CA-D-637-CORE_META_MODEL-CORE--carry-a-formal-graph-rule-as-yaml-with-a-readable-summary.md) names the type but does not yet admit its schema or a Selection resolver.

The named Selection means all Current original logical Atoms in the selected source of truth. Exclude Drafts, archived originals and projection copies. Include Current statuses such as Done and Canceled, not only Active. Classify archival membership from the authoritative lifecycle/placement rules, not preserved historical Status bytes alone. Count logical Atoms, not file/folder representations or repeated source references. An unknown or incomplete population is unresolved, not a passing empty set.

The uniqueness key is canonical Atom.ID alone, never ID plus Version. Archived versions can reuse a canonical ID at different Versions without joining this population.

Sources: [CA-D-446@17](../../07_delivery/CA-D-446-CORE_META_MODEL-CORE--give-every-non-draft-atom-revision-one-identifier.md), [CA-D-378@16](../../07_delivery/CA-D-378-CORE_META_MODEL--serialize-assigned-atom-identities.md) and [CA-D-570@12](../../07_delivery/CA-D-570-CORE_META_MODEL-DELIVERY--serialize-draft-revision-lineage.md). [Project Configuration CA-D-305@16](../../../003_PROJECT_CONFIGURATION/07_delivery/CA-D-305-PROJECT_CONFIGURATION-CORE--carry-projected-atoms-without-new-identity.md) is a concrete example of projected members retaining source identity, not an extra universal Core authority.

# Summary

Keep Current RMED-to-RMED relation targets Current

```yaml
graph_rule_type: endpoint_constraint
applies_to:
  relation: direct
  source:
    lifecycle_group: Current
    content_role:
      - Requirement
      - Method
      - Evaluation
      - Delivery
  target:
    content_role:
      - Requirement
      - Method
      - Evaluation
      - Delivery
condition:
  target_lifecycle_group: Current
  on_unresolved_endpoint_lifecycle: unresolved
```

## Details

The `endpoint_constraint` mapping is proposed only. [CA-D-637@5](../../07_delivery/CA-D-637-CORE_META_MODEL-CORE--carry-a-formal-graph-rule-as-yaml-with-a-readable-summary.md) does not yet admit an endpoint-constraint schema.

Source: [CA-R-1676@21](../CA-R-1676-CORE_META_MODEL-CORE-REQUIREMENT--keep-rmed-to-rmed-relations-within-active-authority.md). Current is a lifecycle group, not an Atom.Status value: exclude Draft and archived sources; include non-archived Done/Canceled where their role permits those statuses. Use authoritative lifecycle/placement, not historical Status bytes alone. Apply only to direct relations whose source and target roles are both in RMED. Relations involving Operations or other kinds are outside this rule, not implicitly prohibited.

The proposed unresolved-lifecycle outcome covers both endpoints, including source applicability. If either role-qualified endpoint's lifecycle cannot be determined, report unresolved before treating the source as out of scope or the target as conforming. Unknown membership is not a passing or automatically inapplicable case.

# Summary

Keep a default within the governed value's constraints

```yaml
graph_rule_type: value_constraint
applies_to:
  node: Entity/Graph Rule
  property: Entity/Graph Rule.Default Value
condition:
  when_present:
    conforms_to: governed_value_constraints
```

## Details

Proposed Value Constraint encoding, not an admitted schema in CA-D-637@5. This Draft introduces no validator or resolver support.

An absent default has nothing to check. A declared default must satisfy the same applicable value constraints as an explicit governed value. An explicit null is a declared value, not absence; its admissibility depends on the governed value's constraints. This rule selects no concrete default and no cross-rule precedence.

Source: [CA-R-1999@1](../CA-R-1999-CORE_META_MODEL-CORE--define-entity-graph-rule-default-value.md). Its fallback-only meaning remains: resolving a default does not automatically write a value or create a relation. Cardinality rules continue to forbid default_value under the existing Delivery schema.

# Summary

Preserve inherited Status values in narrower Atom kinds

```yaml
graph_rule_type: value_constraint
applies_to:
  node: Entity/Node/Continuant/Atom
  property: Entity/Node/Continuant/Atom.Status
condition:
  allowed_value_domain:
    includes_inherited_values: true
    permits_declared_additions: true
```

## Details

Proposed Value Constraint encoding, not an admitted schema in CA-D-637@5. It constrains source-declared allowed-value domains, not the number of Status values on one Atom. It introduces no resolver or universal rule-merging policy.

Each narrower Atom kind retains its inherited Status values and may admit additional values for its qualified Content Role or Type. Inherited values need not be declared again. This does not replace the qualified domain with a closed global list or decide inheritance for other properties.

Sources: [CA-R-1308@13](../CA-R-1308-CORE_META_MODEL-CORE-REQUIREMENT--resolve-status-domains-from-complete-qualified-paths.md) and [CA-R-1947@3](../CA-R-1947-CORE_META_MODEL-GENERAL--define-atom-status-allowed-values.md). The base values and qualified additions remain owned by those source declarations, not copied into this rule.
